title: The Unexpected 'Yes' that Started It All
excerpt: I never saw this coming. It all started with a simple question from a friend: 'Do you want to apply for an internship?' I wanted to see what the real world felt like.
content:
I never saw this coming. It all started with a simple question from a friend: 'Do you want to apply for an internship?' I said yes—not because I was chasing a title or just trying to tick a box to pass, but because I was hungry for the truth of it all. I wanted to see what the 'real world' felt like. I wanted the full experience—the butterflies, the nervous energy, that rush of adrenaline when you’re waiting to see if your answers actually clicked with the interviewer.

When the interview finally came, I decided to just be myself. I didn't try to hide behind rehearsed lines. I just laid out what I knew, shared my stories, stayed confident, and trusted that I was enough. Because I was so focused on the excitement of the challenge, the pressure didn't really have a chance to take hold.

When they called to tell me I got in, I was over the moon. I felt incredibly lucky, though a part of me felt a pang of guilt for my friend who didn't make it. It’s a bittersweet feeling when you get a win that someone you care about misses out on.

Then came orientation day. That’s when the reality of it all finally hit me. I’ll be honest—I was nervous. Standing in a room full of new faces, knowing I had to open up and connect with all these strangers, felt like a big step. But underneath that nerves, there was this spark of genuine excitement. I know this is the start of a whole new chapter, and I’m ready to see where this journey takes me and my fellow interns.

title: Beyond the Front End: A Surprising Evolution
excerpt: Reflecting on my meeting with Sir Ronald and the transition from frontend to full stack.
content:
Sitting there in the meeting with Sir Ronald, hearing him discuss the road ahead, everything suddenly clicked into place. I started this internship walking in as a Frontend Developer, but I realized I’m going to walk out as a Full Stack Developer. It honestly hasn't fully sunk in yet; I came here expecting to sharpen my design and interface skills, but I’m being challenged to see the whole picture. 

I’ll admit, it’s a lot to process. The thought of stepping out of my comfort zone and diving into the backend feels like a massive leap. I’m naturally a bit nervous about the technical hurdles and the new responsibilities, but at the same time, I’m genuinely excited. This is the kind of growth I was looking for—even if I didn't expect it to happen this quickly. I’m ready to embrace the challenge and learn everything I can, knowing that by the time I reach the end of this journey, I’ll be a much more capable and well-rounded developer.
